name: Why is Panchakarma expensive? What you are really paying for
seo_title: Why Is Panchakarma Expensive? | Sabka Ved Wellness
meta_description: Why does Panchakarma cost more than a spa massage? Oils in litres, fresh herbs, two therapists, doctor supervision and diet. How to judge value, explained.
summary: Panchakarma costs more than a massage because it is a doctor-planned medical programme, not a single session. The real drivers are litres of classical oil and ghee, freshly prepared herbal materials, therapist hours, single-patient linen and hygiene, several days of treatment and a doctor who assesses and supervises you throughout.

at_a_glance.typical_session: Most procedures run 45 to 90 minutes including preparation
at_a_glance.typical_course: Programmes usually run 7 to 21 days, decided after assessment

body_html:
It is one of the most common questions people bring to an Ayurvedic consultation: "A massage parlour charges a few hundred rupees, so why does Panchakarma cost so much more?" It is a fair question, and the honest answer is that the two are not the same product. A massage is one hour of touch. Panchakarma, as the classical texts describe it, is a sequence of preparation, cleansing and recovery that runs over days, uses medicines in quantities most people never see, and needs a qualified doctor watching how your body responds.

This guide explains, line by line, where the money in a genuine Panchakarma programme goes. We will not quote figures here, because the right programme for one person can look very different from the right one for another. What we can do is show you the cost drivers so that you can compare any centre, including ours, with clear eyes.

First, what exactly are you buying?

The word Panchakarma means "five actions". Charaka Samhita and Ashtanga Hridaya name them as vamana (therapeutic emesis), virechana (purgation), two kinds of basti (medicated enema) and nasya (nasal therapy), with Sushruta adding raktamokshana (bloodletting) in the surgical tradition. Around these sit purva karma, the preparatory phase of internal oleation, oil massage and sweating, and paschat karma, the graded diet and rejuvenation that follow.

So when you pay for Panchakarma you are paying for a medical plan with three phases, not for a menu item. A centre that sells "Panchakarma" as a single one-hour oil massage is selling something else under a classical name. That difference is the single biggest reason prices vary so widely across Bihar and the rest of India.

The seven real cost drivers

1. Oils, ghee and medicines in litres, not millilitres

A full-body abhyanga uses a generous quantity of warm medicated oil. Pizhichil, where warm oil is poured continuously over the body, uses several litres per sitting, and classical practice is to use fresh oil or carefully reuse it only within strict limits. Shirodhara needs a steady stream for 30 to 45 minutes. Snehapana, the internal oleation before cleansing, uses medicated ghee in rising doses over several days. These oils and ghees are prepared by long processes described in texts such as Sharangadhara Samhita, where herbs are boiled down with oil and liquid until the right consistency is reached. Good classical oils from licensed manufacturers cost real money, and cutting quantity or quality is the easiest way for a cheap package to save money.

2. Freshly prepared herbal materials

Many procedures depend on things that cannot sit on a shelf. Niruha basti uses a freshly made decoction, honey, salt, oil and herbal paste mixed in a classical order on the day. Pinda sweda uses boluses of herbs or rice cooked in milk and decoction, and Navara kizhi boluses are prepared fresh for each session. Dhanyamla for dhara is fermented over days. Takra dhara needs medicated buttermilk made that morning. Each of these takes kitchen time, ingredients and a trained person to prepare.

3. Therapist hours, often two at a time

Synchronised abhyanga and pizhichil are traditionally done by two therapists working in rhythm on either side of the body. A single procedure can involve 15 minutes of preparation, 45 to 90 minutes of treatment and time for cleaning, rest and steam afterwards. Multiply that by a course of seven, fourteen or twenty-one days and the human time becomes the largest line in any honest budget.

4. Doctor assessment and supervision

Before any cleansing, a qualified Ayurvedic physician has to examine you: digestion, bowel pattern, sleep, medicines you take, blood pressure, current illnesses, and whether you are even fit for shodhana (cleansing) at this time. During vamana, virechana or basti, the doctor decides doses, reads the signs of adequate response (samyak lakshana) and manages any discomfort. At Sabka Ved Wellness this is done by Dr. Aditya Kunal, BAMS, who plans every programme himself. That time is part of the cost, and it is also the part you should least want removed.

5. Multi-day programmes

Classical Panchakarma unfolds over time. Snehapana alone can take three to seven days. Virechana is followed by a graded diet called samsarjana krama that can take several more days. Basti courses are traditionally given in sets of eight, fifteen or thirty. A real programme is therefore a booking of many days of treatment rooms, staff and materials, not one appointment.

6. Diet and kitchen

The texts treat food as part of treatment. Peya (thin rice gruel), vilepi (thicker gruel), yusha (lentil soup) and other preparations are introduced in a fixed order after cleansing to rebuild digestion. Whether a centre prepares these itself or guides you closely on what to cook at home, someone has to plan, explain and check this phase.

7. Hygiene, linen and laundry

Oil-soaked towels, sheets and cloths cannot simply be wiped down. Each patient needs fresh linen for every session, and oily linen needs heavy washing. Droni (the treatment table), dhara pots and basti equipment must be cleaned thoroughly between patients. Disposable items for basti and other internal procedures are single-use. Good hygiene is unglamorous and it costs money every single day.

What does research say about whether it is worth it?

We will be straight with you: Panchakarma has been studied far less than it deserves, and much of the published work is small. An observational study of a five-day Panchakarma programme from the Osher Research Center at Harvard Medical School followed 20 women and found that the programme did not significantly improve their overall quality of life score, while self-efficacy, positive health behaviours, perceived social support and depression scores improved, some of them at three months. A 2016 study in Scientific Reports reported changes in blood metabolite profiles in healthy adults after a Panchakarma-based programme. These are early signals, not proof of any cure, and we present them that way. Value, in practice, comes from a programme that matches your needs and is done properly, not from a promise.

Red flags in very cheap Panchakarma packages

  • No doctor before treatment. If you are booked straight onto a table without anyone asking about your medicines, blood pressure, pregnancy or digestion, walk away.
  • "Panchakarma" that is only massage and steam. Abhyanga and swedana are preparation. If no cleansing procedure is planned, ask what the five actions in your package actually are.
  • Same package for everyone. A fixed seven-day plan sold identically to a 25-year-old athlete and a 60-year-old with diabetes is not classical practice.
  • Unlabelled oils. Ask which oil is being used and who made it. Good centres can tell you.
  • Reused linen or shared oil. Ask how linen is handled and how oil reuse, if any, is managed.
  • Cure promises. Anyone who guarantees a cure for diabetes, thyroid disease, infertility or arthritis is breaking the law in India and should not be trusted with your health.
  • No aftercare plan. Cleansing without a graded diet and follow-up can leave people weak and confused. Aftercare is part of the treatment.

How to judge value, not just price

When you compare centres in Patna or anywhere else, ask these questions and listen to the answers:

  1. Who will assess me, and what is their qualification? (In India, look for BAMS or higher, registered under NCISM.)
  2. Which of the five actions do you think I need, and why?
  3. Which preparation and recovery days come with it?
  4. Which oils and medicines will you use, and in roughly what form?
  5. How many therapists, and how long is each session?
  6. What happens if I feel unwell during treatment?
  7. What diet will I follow afterwards, and will you follow up?

A centre that answers clearly is showing you where your money goes. A centre that avoids the questions is telling you something too.

What you seeWhat it usually means
Doctor consultation before any bookingThe programme is planned for you
Different lengths for different peopleClassical, individual planning
Named oils and freshly prepared materialsMedicine quantities are not being cut
Clear contraindication screeningSafety is taken seriously
Written diet and follow-upRecovery is part of the plan

How Sabka Ved Wellness handles cost

At our centre near Bajrang Puri, Patna, nobody is put on a package before a consultation. Dr. Aditya Kunal first assesses you, with particular attention to gut and metabolic health, which is his clinical focus. Many people do not need a full cleansing programme at all; some need only a few external therapies, some need preparation for a later season, and a few should not have shodhana right now. You are told which, and why.

When a programme is advised, you get a plain explanation of what it includes: the procedures, the number of days, the medicines and the aftercare, so you know what you are paying for before you commit. If you are travelling from elsewhere in Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh or Delhi, you can begin with an online consultation and plan one well-organised trip to Patna.

The cheapest Panchakarma is the one you did not need. The most expensive is the one done badly. Our job is to tell you which programme, if any, is right for you.

Book a consultation first

If you are weighing up the cost of Panchakarma, the most useful first step is an assessment, not a package. Request a slot through our appointment page or book directly at superprofile.bio/bookings/dradityakunal. Bring your reports and your list of medicines, and keep taking them as prescribed; nothing changes until you and your own doctors agree.
faqs: Why is Panchakarma more expensive than an Ayurvedic massage?

A massage is one session. Panchakarma is a doctor-planned programme of preparation, cleansing and recovery over several days, using litres of medicated oil and ghee, freshly prepared herbal materials, often two therapists, single-patient linen and continuous medical supervision.
Is a cheap Panchakarma package a bad idea?

Not always, but check what is included. If there is no doctor assessment, no actual cleansing procedure, unlabelled oils or no aftercare plan, the package is usually cheap because those parts are missing.
Does Sabka Ved Wellness publish fixed Panchakarma prices?

Programmes are planned after consultation because different people need very different procedures and durations. After Dr. Aditya Kunal assesses you, the plan and what it includes are explained clearly before you decide.
Can I do only part of Panchakarma to reduce cost?
Sometimes a short course of external therapies or a single procedure is what you actually need. Whether that is appropriate depends on your assessment, which is why consultation comes first.

Research on Panchakarma is still limited and mostly small studies, so nobody can honestly promise results. Value comes from a programme that suits your condition, is done classically and is followed by proper diet and aftercare.
